critical_code_review_comments: check_scheduled_campaigns auto-resume only flips status to 'running' but does NOT itself reset the account's daily_send_count — that reset happens lazily inside process_campaign_queue (line ~5130). The PRD asked the scheduler to 'also reset that account's daily_send_count'. Functionally correct (reset still happens before any send), but the request is technically out-of-scheduler. Consider doing the reset in the same updates_one for atomicity if observability matters.

process_campaign_queue is spawned via asyncio.create_task on a campaign whose 'is_locked' was just set true, but the auto-resume path does NOT clear is_locked on completion failure. A stale orphan worker that exits abnormally could leave is_locked=True. Existing top-of-loop guard `campaign['status'] != 'running'` prevents double-spawn (good), but locks should be released on exception.
server.py is now ~6304 lines. Reiterating prior review: split routers (campaigns, drips, accounts, lists) into modules.

Auto-resume cycle is 30s and reads ALL paused_daily_limit campaigns + their accounts on every tick — fine at low scale but could become an N+M query per tick at 100s of orgs. Consider an index on campaigns.status and aggregating per-user.
